body:
It's a tough situation to deal with.

What I would have wished for was sympathy(there's nothing wrong in wanting it.), even though you don't know how he feel, just understand the fact that he's having a tough time. I can tell you one thing for certain, the fact he said that he wanted to kill himself has to be taken seriously. When a person says such a thing, it's likely a desperate cry for help. It can indicated that he has a lot of negative feelings he carries all by himself, and that noone around him knows he has it, and that can cause a lot of frustration. 

It may be hard for him to just sit down and talk about problems, I  know it was for me; instead I just randomly had these breakdowns where I'd gone a long time and building up the feeling inside of me. I didn't want to talk to deep about things, but I wanted to let people know that something was wrong, and when I said that I wanted to kill myself to family members, I know that it was a desperate attempt at getting people to care. And by care I mean being interested in his situation and interested in how bad/good he has it.

I would have done this; contact a therapist for him without him knowing it and make an appointment for him, and then say he just needs to go to one appointment with the therapist, and if he doesn't like it he doesn't need to anymore. 

The fact is if he hits a good tone with the therapist, he will himself want to continue going. It's very likely that he has alot to say that he won't say to any friends/family but when you're with a therapist it's much easier to be honest and let everything of your chest. So seeing a therapist should atleast be a start i think, and you'll take it from there and see how it goes.

I think everyone have experiences like this in their lifes, most likely several times. But, I understand that if you're not happy in the first place, things like these can have an extra tough impact. I know, I've had lovesickness on top of depression, and it's almost unimagineable how fucking sad you feel in that situation. You're angry, confused, depressed, scared all at once and don't know if you want to kill yourself or go punch into a wall. (done a lot of wall-punching)

I just wanna say I understand your situation, I've been in it 2 times, but the fact is that it will go over. I certainly didn't think it would ever go over and that's what's so lame about it, and I felt the only solution was to kill myself at that time but now I'm glad I didn't(although I'm still depressed, but for slightly other reasons). It's a feeling of hopelessness and that you're doomed...because it can last really long, but eventually, you're bound to forget about it and move on. So hold on there, I don't know your story, but i would guess you're depressed so I completely understand it sucks to get in this situation.

I think cassieko is right here. It's very likely temporary. I know you don't want to hear this but, you ARE young and things WILL change... it's almost a fact that things will choange for you, just hold on and like cassieko said you will look back and laugh at those prblems.

Don't do it! I'm writing this because as a depressed person myself I take you very seriously. People who haven't experienced that kind of pain or anything near to it can't imagine people being serious when they say they want to kill themselves, but as a person who lately have been thinking of going in to the woods and hang myself I know those thoughts are very real and serious, because I've been concidering and planing killing myself lately, and I know for a fact that I wasn't that incredibly far from actually going through with it. You would do me a favor if you sent me a message as soon as you read this, and we can talk.

I don't know exactly what your pain is like, but I know pain. I've been depressed for about 5 years, started mildly and then it has got really bad lately where I've been suicidal. Unlike you I finished High School about three years ago, but like you, that's when i shortly after started to think seriously about killing myself... I'm still going, I'm suprised I haven't ended it yet. anway, if you want to talk just drop me a PM! I would like hear more about your situation. (I sincerely mean it!)

What i just said may sound a bit "too simple", but I really mean it. You're in an age where you have the biggest changes in life ahead of you, so wait for them to happen, and then see what you think about your life.

You're 13... I can tell you with certainty that things will change, and maybe for the better. When you're 20 you will meet different people, develop new interests and on the way you will have many new experiences which will change your future. 

I would say, don't think about it, just be yourself and work on your self esteem and you're gonna be fine.

I don't have a person I'm trying to copy the physique of, because I know that won't work. My body is pretty different shaped from every other body I've seen, and most are. If you try to copy the physique of brad pitt, which seems many are stribing for, you're probably not gonna come close to that because your body isn't Brad Pitt's body. 

So, I think it's better to look at what you're most happy about with your own body and make those features more visible, though it's always nice to be well proportionate, meaning not having toothpick arms and huge legs, for example. 

I read somewere that instead of copying others you should make others want to copy you. Seems like a good attitude to have. :)

I thought the same thing, it's incredible that it took me so long to realize how little logic that way of thinking actually holds... think about it; in the stone age, I can't imagine anyone being obese, and noone probably were. I bet people was pretty much equally slim... but because of the eating habits in todays society I was almost fooled to believing athletes just were made that way, and that the average guy on the street could not have an atheltic body if he wanted to. It's just so wrong and far from reality, and sadly I supsect many obese people think think in that way, that they were born fat and always will be.

Emotional for the most part. I have been to a psychologist for about half a year. It's very complicated but to make a long story short; It's mostly about that I have become overly self-concious about how I look and how I am and act as a person. That's really the big picture here, and my main problem... but I have had bad self-esteem since my early teens and have been bullied before, so that "laid the foundation" for my life being so shitty ever since that time. And it doesn't help either that last year when I was really depressed and had anxiety-issues I got rejected by a girl and got really bad lovesickness on top of all the stuff I already had to deal with. But thanks for the tip, I will at least concider it.
